messages.subject: Project to New Extent
messages.body_plain:
Hi, everyone,

I seem to be having an issue with projecting to a new spatial extent. I'm new to species distribution modeling and am working on this for my Master's thesis.

I was able to successfully run the model and project to a new extent; however, the entire extent I selected isn't projected. I am projecting a species into the southern United States, including Florida, and so far, I can draw a polygon fairly far north, but the habitat suitability does not show up at all for Florida, past Jacksonville. Based on the map, I can see a lot of high suitability areas right along the cut off that appear to extend, but the map always slices off, no matter how far south I extend the polygon. Does anyone know what might be going on?

Thank you!
Kelly

messages.subject: Re: Project to New Extent
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kelly,
What resolution were you using for the environmental data?
I ask because 30arcsec is served by a single tile. From the picture, it looks like it is predicting as much of the extent as the tile covers, and then stops short. Wallace will only load one tile, but the other option is to go to the environmental data website and download a larger extent, and use the files with the "User Upload" module.
-Bethany

messages.subject: Re: Multi-species and Multitemporal species distribution habitat maps
messages.subject_clean: Multi-species and Multitemporal species distribution habitat maps
messages.body_plain:
Wallace can only use a single band at a time, so each year will need to be run separately.
And importing a table like this into Step 6 is not possible.

On Monday, April 25, 2022 at 10:03:57 AM UTC-4 rubened...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi Wallace team!,
>
> I am using Wallace to create species distribution maps in the Gran Chaco accross time (1985 -2020). The study focus on mutiple mammals species also. I am using the Wallace v1.9 version, where I have succesufully enter the occurrence dataset "csv" with multiple species.
>
> In addition to this, I have 10 predictor rasters (environmental and land use data) in tiff format, in which within each raster is contained 36 bands, that is, each year.
>
> I would like to try to use the multiple species and the multitemporal predictors tiffs, thus a main table cotaning the value for each occurrence for each predictor and year, would be created. Would it be this possible?
>
> Alternatively, I have already the final tables with all values for each predictor (occurrence and background points) . Would it be possible to enter this tables from step 6? where the user can use Maxent module?
>
> Any comment/suggestion would be greatly appreciated! ,
>
> Thank you in advance,
>
> Best,
>
> Rubén
>
>
>
>
messages.body_snippet:
Wallace can only use a single band at a time, so each year will need to be run separately.
And importing a table like this into Step 6 is not possible.

Thanks!
